div.head: II Eg 5.2
div.ab: ⁊ læste man saulsceat æt ælcan Cristenan men to þam mynstre, þe hit togebyrige.
⁊ gelæste man sawlsceat æt ælcan Cristenan men to ðam mynstre, þe hit togebirige.
⁊ gelæste man sawlsceat æt ælcan Cristenan men to ðam mynstre þe hit togebirige.
And læste man saulsceat æt ælcan Cristenan men to þam mynstre þe hit togebyrige.
(Und man leiste Seelengeld von jedem [verstorbenen] Christenmenschen an die Kirche, der es zukommt. A D)
(And let soul-scot be paid for every [deceased] Christian man to the minster to which it belongs. A D)
And payment for the souls of the dead shall be rendered to the church to which it is due on behalf of every Christian man.
[And payment for the soul is to be paid for every Christian man to the minster to which it belongs.
And dues for the souls of the dead are to be paid on behalf of every Christian to the church to which they are owed.

note.seg: Die Sätze 5, 2; 3 scheinen laut klerikalen Inhaltes eher Zufügung eines geistlichen Abschreibers als durch einen solchen fortgelassen. Hieraus V Atr 12, 1 = VI 21. I Cn 13. Vgl. Gl Seelschatz 2. a

Clauses 5, 2; 3, to judge by their clerical content, seem more likely to be an addition by a clerical copyist than to have been omitted by one. From them derive V Atr 12, 1 = VI 21. I Cn 13. Cf. Gl Seelschatz 2. a
Every member of the parish; see Wb: cristen 3

§ 2 and § 3. Liebermann is of opinion that these clauses are more likely to have been added to the original text by ecclesiastical scribes in the case of MSS A and D than to have been omitted by such a copyist in the case of MS G.
